claim: The typical subthreshold response to activation of fan cell inputs in L2 SCs and L2 PCs was biphasic, with an initial EPSP followed by an IPSP.

claim: EPSPs were largest in L2 PCs on average compared to L2 SCs and principal cells in L3, L5a, and L5b.

claim: The latency of responses of L2 SCs and L2 PCs were generally short suggesting they result from direct monosynaptic inputs.

claim: The EPSPs evoked in L2 SCs and L2 PCs were abolished by the AMPA receptor antagonist NBQX and NMDA receptor antagonist AP-5.

evidence: This is stated as a finding from the pharmacology experiments shown in Figure 5A-B.

claim: EPSPs evoked by fan cell inputs in L2 SCs and L2 PCs are glutamatergic.

claim: The EPSPs showed low variation in their latencies.
source: Consistent with their reflecting direct monosynaptic activation, the EPSPs showed low variation in their latencies (Figure 5C–D), and following abolition by application of tetrodotoxin (TTX) could be recovered by further application of 4-aminopyridine (4-AP; Figure 5E–F).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the pharmacology experiments shown in Figure 5C-D.

claim: Following abolition by application of tetrodotoxin (TTX), EPSPs could be recovered by further application of 4-aminopyridine (4-AP).

claim: Inhibitory components of responses to optogenetic activation of fan cell axons require excitation of intermediary neuronal populations.

evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the pharmacology experiments shown in Figure 5A-B.

claim: Bath application of GABA receptor antagonists had a modest effect on EPSP amplitudes.

claim: E-I ratios were greater on average for L2 PCs compared to L2 SCs.
source: E-I ratios, calculated as the amplitude of the EPSP normalised to the total amplitude of the EPSP and IPSP, were greater on average for L2 PCs compared to L2 SCs (W=1233.5, p=0.034, Wilcoxon test), with almost all L2 PCs showing a greater net excitation, whereas the L2 SC population was more heterogeneous and included neurons that showed greater net inhibition as well as neurons that favoured excitation (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the analysis of E-I ratios shown in Figure 9A.

claim: Almost all L2 PCs showed a greater net excitation in response to fan cell activation.
source: E-I ratios, calculated as the amplitude of the EPSP normalised to the total amplitude of the EPSP and IPSP, were greater on average for L2 PCs compared to L2 SCs (W=1233.5, p=0.034, Wilcoxon test), with almost all L2 PCs showing a greater net excitation, whereas the L2 SC population was more heterogeneous and included neurons that showed greater net inhibition as well as neurons that favoured excitation (Figure 9A).

claim: For L2 SCs and L2 PCs, the E-I ratio of the membrane potential responses to activation of fan cell inputs did not vary with neuronal location on the mediolateral or dorsoventral axis of MEC.

evidence: This is stated as a finding from the analysis of E-I ratios and neuron position shown in Figure 9E-F.

claim: The heterogeneity of L2 SC responses and the excitatory bias of L2 PCs were both maintained during 10 Hz stimulation.
source: We find that the striking heterogeneity of L2 SC responses, and the bias of L2 PC responses towards excitation, were both maintained (Figure 10A–D).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the 10 Hz stimulation experiments shown in Figure 10.

claim: For individual L2 SCs and L2 PCs, the relative bias towards excitation was similar for responses at the start and end of the 10 Hz train.

claim: EPSP responses of L2 principal neurons to input from fan cells are mediated by monosynaptic glutamatergic excitation.
source: Together, these experiments demonstrate that EPSP responses of L2 principal neurons to input from fan cells are mediated by monosynaptic glutamatergic excitation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the pharmacology experiments.

claim: IPSP responses of L2 principal neurons to fan cell inputs are indirect and are consistent with glutamatergic excitation of interneuron populations.
source: In contrast, IPSP responses are indirect and are consistent with glutamatergic excitation of interneuron populations; this could in principle arise from feedforward excitation of interneuron populations by fan cell inputs or by recurrent feedback excitation following spiking by L2 principal cells.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the pharmacology experiments.

claim: Interneurons in L1 and L2 of the MEC receive powerful excitatory input from LEC fan cells that is effective at driving spiking.
source: Together, these data demonstrate that interneurons in L1 and L2 of the MEC receive powerful excitatory input from LEC fan cells that is effective at driving spiking.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the optogenetic stimulation experiments.

claim: L1 interneurons mediate slow inhibitory inputs to layer 2 principal cells in the MEC.
source: We also show that L1 interneurons mediate slow inhibitory inputs to layer 2 principal cells in the MEC.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the paired recording experiments.

claim: Fan cells drive feedforward inhibitory input to principal cells in layer 2, with L1 interneurons mediating slow inhibitory components.
source: Thus, our data support a circuit model in which fan cells drive feedforward inhibitory input to principal cells in layer 2, with L1 interneurons mediating slow inhibitory components.
